City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 18, 2022
  1
   City Council Regular Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, October 18, 2022

 •  CALL TO ORDER
 •  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Council Member Wu
 •  ROLL CALL: Mayor Ding, Vice Mayor Harrington, Council Members Menchaca,
  Rivera, Wu

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. INTRODUCTION AND PROMOTION OF FIRE ENGINEER BRENT PATTISON

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. RESOLUTION NO. 22-67 REAUTHORIZING THE CITY COUNCIL AND THE
  CITY’S COMMISSIONS TO IMPLEMENT TELECONFERENCE ACCCESSIBILITY
  FOR CONDUCTING PUBLIC MEETINGS PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 361

  Resolution No. 22-67 makes findings that allow the City to continue
  implementation of teleconference/internet-based accessibility for public
  meetings under state-of-emergency provisions.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-67 regarding
  the use of teleconferencing for public meetings.

  B. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of October 4, 2022.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of October 4, 2022.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 18, 2022  2
   Recommended Action: Approval.

  C. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are presented
  to the City Council for review and approval.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  D. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – SEPTEMBER 2022

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2022-2023 Adopted Investment
  Policy (Resolution No. 22-30) and California Government Code Section 53646,
  the Finance Director is to render an investment report to the City Council, City
  Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney. The September 2022 Cash and
  Investment Report is presented to receive and file in accordance with the City’s
  adopted 2022-23 Investment Policy.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the staff report.

  E. MONTHLY BUDGET UPDATE – SEPTEMBER 2022

  This report provides a monthly budget update for the City’s General Fund and
  Mission Playhouse as of September 30, 2022. The monthly budget update
  incorporates the actual revenue received and expenditures that have occurred
  through September 30, 2022, and projects the financial results for the year
  ending June 30, 2023. There is no fiscal impact related to this item.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the report.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 18, 2022  3
   F. FISCAL YEAR 2021-22 YEAR-END APPROPRIATION ADJUSTMENTS

  At year end, budget adjustments for the prior Fiscal Year are needed to add
  appropriations to departments or funds that have exceeded the original
  appropriation. This report requests Council’s approval for budget adjustments
  to transfer appropriations between departments or to a fund that has exceeded
  the current budgeted appropriations, along with explanations for the
  adjustments. There is no fiscal impact related to this item.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-66 approving
  proposed amendments to the annual budget for the Fiscal Year 2021-22.

  G. RESOLUTION NO. 22-59 APPROVING A REQUEST FOR TEMPORARY
  STREET CLOSURE ON THE 800 BLOCK OF COMMERCIAL AVENUE

  The Public Works Department received a request from Jason De La Torre, owner
  at 864 Commercial Avenue, for a temporary street closure. The purpose of this
  request is to hold a block party for a 4th Anniversary Celebration for Ogopogo
  Brewing. The block party will be held on Saturday, November 5, 2022, on the
  800 block of Commercial Avenue from 2:00 p.m. to 10:00 p.m. Ogopogo has
  had four prior street closure events and the City has not experienced any
  significant adverse issues from those prior events. Fees are not charged for
  these services, and budgeted Public Works staff time will be used for the street
  closure.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Resolution No. 22-59
  authorizing closure on the 800 block of Commercial Avenue from South Gladys
  Avenue to the end of the cul-de-sac from 2:00 p.m. to 10:00 p.m. on Saturday,
  November 5, 2022.

  H. APPROVAL OF FINAL TRACT MAP AND SUBDIVISION IMPROVEMENT
  AGREEMENT FOR TRACT NO. 73409 (PROPOSED MIXED-USE
  DEVELOPMENT AT 101 EAST VALLEY BOULEVARD, “THE ONE”)

  The project located at 101 East Valley Boulevard, is a four-story mixed-use
  development with approximately 13,500 square feet of commercial space and
  81 residential condominium units on an 86,917 square feet (0.86 acres) site.
  Staff and the City’s contract consultant for land surveying, RKA Consulting

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 18, 2022  4
   Group, Incorporated, have reviewed the Final Tract Map and determined that it
  is in compliance with the State Subdivision Map Act, conditions of approval,
  and the City’s ordinances regarding subdivisions. There is no fiscal impact
  related to this item.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Final Tract Map No. 73409,
  authorize its filing with the Los Angeles County Recorder and authorize the City
  Manager to execute the Subdivision Agreement on behalf of the City.

  I. RESOLUTION NO. 22-63 RATIFYING THE MEMORANDUM OF
  UNDERSTANDING WITH THE SAN GABRIEL POLICE MANAGEMENT
  GROUP FOR THE JULY 1, 2022 THROUGH JUNE 30, 2025 PERIOD AND
  INCREASING GENERAL FUND APPROPRIATIONS FOR POLICE
  MANAGEMENT SALARIES

  In May 2022, the City and San Gabriel Police Management Group (PMG)
  entered into negotiations for a successor Memorandum of Understanding
  (MOU). The most recent MOU between the City and PMG expired on June 30,
  2022. Representatives of the City and PMG have reached a tentative agreement
  on a three-year successor MOU for the July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2025
  period, subject to City Council approval. The three-year successor MOU with
  the PMG is expected to have a total three-year cost impact of $981,921, of
  which $227,486 is for FY 2022-23, $351,235 is for FY 2023-24, and $403,200 is
  for FY 2024-25.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-63, which ratifies
  the three-year successor MOU for the period covering July 1, 2022 through
  June 30, 2025 between the City and PMG, and appropriates $227,486 in General
  Funds for increased Police personnel salaries; and authorize the City’s
  negotiators to execute the MOU.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 18, 2022  5
   A. DISCUSSION AND INPUT ON CITY COUNCIL RECOGNITION POLICY

  On April 1, 2013, Administrative Policy 309 – Recognition Guidelines was
  established by staff members to guide how the City recognizes and
  congratulates the many contributions made by members of the community,
  City organizations, and businesses. The existing policy governs how
  proclamations, certificates, commendations, and City tiles are utilized. Staff is
  seeking input and direction on an update to the policy, eventually to be brought
  back at a future meeting and adopted as the official recognition policy for the
  City of San Gabriel. There is no fiscal impact to discuss and provide input on
  the City’s recognition policy.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council discuss the current recognition policy
  and provide input on a revised policy to be brought back at a future City Council
  meeting for consideration.

  B. GRAPEVINE GUIDE AND GRAPEVINE NEWSLETTER MERGE

  The City of San Gabriel produces two publications, Grapevine Guide and Grapevine
  Newsletter, that are each released four times a year, for a total of eight publications a
  year. Staff is seeking Council’s approval to combine the two publications into one
  consolidated publication, develop a new name and updated theme, and release a
  request for proposal for printing and design services accordingly. Fiscal impact will be
  determined once the results of the requests for proposals for printing and mailing
  services and design services have been reviewed.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the merge of the Grapevine Guide
  and Grapevine Newsletter with a new name of “Discover San Gabriel” and allow staff
  to begin working on the process of creating a new design and cohesive magazine for
  release in Spring 2023.

 8. PUBLIC COMMENT

 9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

 10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 18, 2022  6
   Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

  11. CLOSED SESSION – None.

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, November 1, 2022

  A. DISCUSSION AND INPUT ON CITY COUNCIL RECOGNITION POLICY

  City Manager Lazzaretto made the presentation .

I  Chasity Jennings-Nunez, resident, spoke in favor of proclamations and certificates
  being signed by all Council Members, and in favor of the one-week-prior request
  deadline, and requested that the policy include language detailing standing
  proclamations.

  Discussion included that the City website already has a list of standing
  proclamations and possible related wording for the policy; the Mayor would
  approve new proclamations, or a majority of Council could override the Mayor;
  definition of milestone birthdays; preference for certificates from the entire

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 3 of 4  October 18, 2022
   Council; adding information about the research and approval component s of the
  process into the policy; commendation to the City Clerk Department for
  personalizing certificates; addition of verbiage about the vetting process on the
  City's website page; the process for distributing certificates; including a point of
  contact on the website page; fiscal impact for staff time; process for duplicate
  requests; letters of commendation from individual Council Members as long as
  they don't speak for entire Council; copying the entire Council on letters sent by
  the Mayor; and clarifying language in the policy to distinguish ceremonial content
  versus legislative support.

I  There was a consensus of the City Council to direct staff to prepare a policy for City
  Council consideration incorporating the components discussed.

  Council Member Rivera announced the Fall Festival on October 28, 2022, and the
